q-161747.name: Question 1
q-161747.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161747.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $4$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 4,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}y\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 4 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤4,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=yx2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ=ρ2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Ryx2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ2sin⁡θsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫04ρ4sin⁡θsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161756.name: Question 2
q-161756.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=\frac{1}{9}.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161756.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\frac{1}{3}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \frac{1}{3},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}+{(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{yz}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ}{\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1/3}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

q-161757.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2$ for $y\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161757.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224175/assets/6f35be4fd6773149597ea8a9dc8dd234e068da3f0fd3b2df32d11c61521bed75.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{2},\,\pi \le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )} \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\sqrt{{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ} \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}z\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

a

c

EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents one-half of the sphere of radius 2 centered at the origin.

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤2,π≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=zx2+y2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=ρcos⁡ϕ(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2+(ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ)2=ρcos⁡ϕρ2cos2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ+ρ2sin2⁡θsin2⁡ϕ=ρcos⁡ϕρ2sin2⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+sin2⁡θ)=ρcos⁡ϕρ2sin2⁡ϕ=ρ2cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭Rzx2+y2dV=∭Δρ2cos⁡ϕsin⁡ϕ⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫π2π∫02ρ4cos⁡ϕsin2⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

q-161760.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16$ for $x\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161760.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $4$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224175/assets/8c803dbf5bcf6c2ece6c1c8352f96da1c88734ca1d792dd05593ac8c11527b2b.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 4,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ((\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ({\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ({\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )) \\  & =2\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ({\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ) \\  & =2{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}2x({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}2{\rho }^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{4}2{\rho }^{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{4}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

q-161761.name: Question 5
q-161761.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=5.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
q-161761.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\sqrt{5}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{5},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}(x+z)\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{5}}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ+\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

The region R is enclosed inside the sphere x2+y2+z2=5. Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. ∭R(x+z)x2+y2+z2dV

a
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
b
∫02π∫02π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕ(cos2⁡θ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
c
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ3sin⁡ϕcos⁡θ(sin⁡ϕ+1)dρdθdϕ
d
∫02π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+sin⁡θcos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ
e
∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4(sin⁡ϕ+cos⁡θ)dρdθdϕ
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

∭Rf(x,y,z)dV=∭Δf(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ.

If (ρ,θ,ϕ) are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates (x,y,z) can be found by using the following formulas:

x=ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,y=ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,z=ρcos⁡ϕ

Notice that the region R represents the sphere of radius 5 centered at the origin. As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as

Δ={(ρ,θ,ϕ):0≤ρ≤5,0≤θ≤2π,0≤ϕ≤π}.

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function f(x,y,z)=(x+z)x2+y2+z2:

f(x,y,z)=f(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρsin⁡θsin⁡ϕ,ρcos⁡ϕ)=(ρcos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+ρcos⁡ϕ)⋅ρ=ρ2(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

∭R(x+z)x2+y2+z2dV=∭Δρ2(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)⋅ρ2sin⁡ϕdρdθdϕ=∫0π∫02π∫05ρ4sin⁡ϕ(cos⁡θsin⁡ϕ+cos⁡ϕ)dρdθdϕ.
